[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Eka Pada Rajakapotasana (One-Legged King Pigeon Pose) - A challenging hip opener that targets the glutes, hips, and lower back.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Astavakrasana (Eight-Angled Pose) - A balancing pose that strengthens the arms, legs, and core.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Pincha Mayurasana (Feathered Peacock Pose) - An inverted balance pose that targets the arms, shoulders, and core.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Hanumanasana (Monkey Pose) - A deep forward bend that stretches the hamstrings, calves, and spine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Supta Baddha Konasana (Reclined Bound Angle Pose) - A relaxing pose that stretches the hips, thighs, and lower back.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested new yoga flows:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Sun Salutations with a Twist - Add a twist to traditional Sun Salutations by incorporating a twist in Downward-Facing Dog or Warrior II.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Balancing Flow - Focus on balancing poses like Eagle, Tree, and Crow to improve balance and stability.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Hip Opening Flow - Target hips with a flow that includes Pigeon, Lizard, and Camel Pose.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Core Strengthening Flow - Engage core with a flow that includes Boat Pose, Side Plank, and Plank Pose.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Yin-Yang Flow - Alternate between yin (slow, passive) and yang (fast, active) movements to create a balanced practice.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested tips to mix up the yoga routine:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Change Your Focus - Focus on breath, bandha (energy locks), or drishti (focused gaze).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Play with Props - Use blocks, straps, or blankets to modify or deepen poses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Try Different Styles - Experiment with different yoga styles, such as Hatha, Vinyasa, Restorative, or Kundalini.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Practice at Different Times - Try practicing at different times of the day or in different environments.
